current: The Census of Israel — Julius Schnorr von Carolsfeld, 1860

fix: Caption: "Inverted nun in the Leningrad Codex, Numbers 10:35–36". Better: move this image to behaalotecha (10:35-36 is in its range) and give bamidbar an image of the census or the camp.

current: The Torah does not date the rebellion; no traditional year given.
problem: True of the Torah, but the file's _about says a parsha without a traditional entry "has no dated event in the Torah or the chronology". Seder Olam Rabbah 8 does place Korah's rebellion straight after the spies (Av of the second year), though it gives no date of its own.
evidence: Seder Olam Rabbah 8 (Sefaria English): "On the Ninth of Av it was decreed...that they would not enter the Land. After the spies was the strife of Korah, and his being swallowed up..." https://www.sefaria.org/Seder_Olam_Rabbah.8
fix: In scripts/buildParshaDates.mjs: korach: { scholarly: 'exodus', note: 'The Torah does not date the rebellion. Seder Olam Rabbah 8 places it right after the spies, who returned on 9 Av of the second year, but gives no date; no traditional year given.' }

current: Miriam and Aaron die, in the 40th year [sources: Numbers 20:1, Numbers 33:38, Chabad "The Exodus"]
problem: The year is right, but the cited sources support it only for Aaron (33:38). Numbers 20:1 says only "the first month" with no year; the 40th year for Miriam's death comes from Seder Olam Rabbah 9, which is not cited.
evidence: Numbers 20:1: "The Israelites arrived in a body at the wilderness of Zin on the first new moon" (the verse gives no year; JPS adds a translator's footnote "Of the fortieth year; cf. 33.36–38"). Numbers 33:38: Aaron died "in the fortieth year after the Israelites had left the land of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month". Seder Olam Rabbah 9: "When the well disappeared, it was Year 40, and it was the first of the month of Nissan". https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.20.1 ; https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.33.38 ; https://www.sefaria.org/Seder_Olam_Rabbah.9
fix: chukat: { scholarly: 'exodus', traditional: t(YEAR40, 'Miriam and Aaron die, in the 40th year', [SEF('Numbers 20:1'), SEF('Numbers 33:38'), SOR(9), CHABAD_EXODUS]) }

current: am 2487, yearBCE 1274, "On the plains of Moab, in the 40th year" [sources: Numbers 33:38, Deuteronomy 1:3, Chabad]
problem: The stay on the plains of Moab runs from after Aaron's death (1 Av, AM 2487) to Moses' last speeches (1 Shevat of the 40th year), which the same script dates to AM 2488 (the Deuteronomy entries use YEAR40 + 1, citing the same Deuteronomy 1:3). Tishrei 2488 begins the new AM year, so a single AM 2487 is too precise; the honest value is a range 2487-2488 (c. 1274-1273 BCE).
evidence: Numbers 33:38: Aaron died "in the fortieth year ... on the first day of the fifth month". Deuteronomy 1:3: "It was in the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, that Moses addressed the Israelites". Seder Olam Rabbah 9 puts the arrival at Arvot Moav after Aaron's death and the wars with Sihon and Og: "The Israelites traveled and encamped at Arvot Mo'av". Script: DEUT entries use t(YEAR40 + 1, ..., [SEF('Deuteronomy 1:3'), ...]). https://www.sefaria.org/Numbers.33.38 ; https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.1.3 ; https://www.sefaria.org/Seder_Olam_Rabbah.9
fix: balak: { scholarly: 'exodus', traditional: t(YEAR40, 'On the plains of Moab, in the 40th year', [SEF('Numbers 33:38'), SOR(9), SEF('Deuteronomy 1:3'), CHABAD_EXODUS], YEAR40 + 1) }  (gives AM 2487–2488, c. 1274–1273 BCE)
